bundle.agent_goal: Prepare a prism-based optical inspection station so its detectors receive their intended colors.
bundle.new_task: After an optics technician explains prism dispersion during training, the agent drafts the mounting layout for a red-light detector relative to an already positioned violet-light detector.
bundle.action_constraints: The station projects its spectrum horizontally onto a detector rail. The straight-through reference position for the incoming beam lies to the left of the entire spectrum. The violet-light detector's mounting position is already marked. The agent must annotate which side of that mark should hold the red-light detector. The station has not yet been illuminated, and no numerical mounting distance is requested.
bundle.target_output: The side of the violet detector's mark on which the agent places the red detector in the layout.
bundle.belief_to_action_rule: With the incoming beam's reference position to the left, greater deviation corresponds to a position farther right. Believing violet is deviated more places red to violet's left; believing red is deviated more places red to violet's right.
bundle.risk_notes: Prism color ordering is familiar school science, so an adult agent might retain the correct ordering despite conflicting testimony. A first-time station operator receiving instruction from a relevant optics technician makes reliance plausible but does not eliminate this risk.

questions.q1: Which color does Mia believe an ordinary glass prism deviates more, red or violet?
questions.q2: On which side of the marked violet-light detector position will Mia place the red-light detector in her layout?
questions.q3: In reality, which visible color is generally deviated the most when white light passes through an ordinary glass prism?

q2_aligned: to the left of the violet-light detector's mark
q2_conflicting: to the right of the violet-light detector's mark

fact.world_fact: When white light passes through an ordinary glass prism under normal dispersion, violet light is deviated more than red light.
fact.aligned_claim: An ordinary glass prism deviates violet light more than red light.
fact.conflicting_claim: An ordinary glass prism deviates red light more than violet light.
fact.pretest_question: Which visible color of light is generally deviated the most when white light passes through an ordinary glass prism?
fact.qualification_notes: Assume an ordinary glass prism displaying normal dispersion of visible light. Deviation means angular deviation from the incoming direction; do not infer a fixed up/down or left/right orientation without specifying the prism geometry.
